tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms and intents (endpoint fails, slow, cold-starts, costs too much, right-sizing questions) rather than internal mechanics, explicitly lists many trigger contexts across real-time, serverless/async, and batch transform scenarios, and clarifies scope boundaries. It is a longer paragraph but proportionate to the breadth of the skill's coverage and remains focused on triggers rather than implementation detail.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when an endpoint is Failed or never passes its health check, cannot read its model artifact from S3 or KMS, is unreachable from a private subnet, returns ModelError or 5xx, does not scale out, or sits idle while billed..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but almost entirely project/domain-specific — check-id tables, router rows, API quirks, and procedural steps. It does not explain generic concepts like what an endpoint or HTTP is; everything is SageMaker-specific operational knowledge the agent wouldn't otherwise have.
tests.evidence: Load checks-sagemaker-inference.md before assigning any check-id or severity... Every finding is grounded in the LLM-SM check family

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps the check catalog as a compact index table and router table (pointers with brief descriptions), while the full detection rules, remediations, and citations live in references/checks-sagemaker-inference.md, which is explicitly loaded before use. No large reference blocks or embedded lookup data are inlined.
tests.evidence: Load [checks-sagemaker-inference.md](references/checks-sagemaker-inference.md) before writing any finding: it holds the full detection rules, remediations, and citations.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All six reference files (api-quirks.md, checks-sagemaker-inference.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, collection-reference.md, known-causes.md, metrics-and-logs.md) are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Every reference link is accompanied by an explicit trigger condition for when to load it (e.g., matching symptom, specific step, specific API response type).
tests.evidence: "load it before assigning any check-id or severity" and "load it whenever the user names an error or symptom"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, order-dependent operations (Review Procedure, Guardrails, Before You Present checklist) are given exact prescriptive steps, while interpretive tasks (fit decision, severity assignment) explain the reasoning ('why') rather than dictating rigid steps.
tests.evidence: "Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist... Every step is best-effort"

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where tool/approach choices exist (e.g., real-time vs serverless vs async vs batch fit decision), the skill gives clear decision criteria rather than presenting equal menus, and router table entries point to one specific API/check as the first read.
tests.evidence: "Whether that traffic belongs on serverless (spiky, low volume, tolerates cold starts) or async (large payloads, long invocations) is LLM-SM-SERVE-005, driven by payload size and invocation duration."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (Review Procedure steps 1-8, router matching, check catalog) applicable to any SageMaker endpoint or job, not a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: "Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist. Each step depends on state gathered by the one before it..."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit 'Common wrong answers' section documenting non-obvious pitfalls and misreadings of API responses, plus an 'Error Handling' section with api-quirks traps — functioning as a gotchas section.
tests.evidence: "The endpoint is `InService`, so it's serving traffic and the queue is fine." ... "Confirm a non-zero instance count, recent `Invocations`..."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces health reports and provides dedicated templates in assets/ for each area, referenced conditionally.
tests.evidence: "[endpoint-health-report-template.md](assets/endpoint-health-report-template.md) — load when a full real-time endpoint report is requested."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline templates exist in the body; the three health-report templates are kept in assets/ and only referenced conditionally.
tests.evidence: Templates are referenced only via links in the 'Step 8' and Appendix sections, not inlined.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three asset files (batch-job-health-report-template.md, endpoint-health-report-template.md, serverless-async-health-report-template.md) are linked in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each asset link specifies the exact trigger condition (which type of report requested) for loading it.
tests.evidence: "load when a full real-time endpoint report is requested", "load when a full serverless or async report is requested", "load when a full batch transform report is requested"

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: All asset references use relative paths of the form assets/<filename>.md.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural Review Procedure section uses the required checkbox checklist format with 'Step N:' naming, and the detailed subsections below it reference the same step numbers (Step 1, Step 2, etc.).
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: Identify the area and enumerate resources." ... "### Step 1 — Identify the area"

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to check its findings, citations, severities and disclosures before presenting.
tests.evidence: "Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion."
